question: Which body fluid is NOT considered potentially infectious under standard precautions?
explanation: Sweat does not transmit bloodborne pathogens and is excluded from standard precaution transmission assumptions. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h1)

question: Why do midwives apply standard precautions to every patient in the maternity ward?

options.A: To prevent infection spread regardless of known infection status
options.B: To eliminate the need for patient medical history
options.D: To reduce the cost of specialized equipment

explanation: Standard precautions treat every person as potentially infectious because many infections are undiagnosed. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h1)

question: What is the term for the path an organism uses to leave its source?
explanation: The portal of exit is the pathway through which a pathogen escapes the reservoir, such as through blood or body fluids. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h2)

question: How do standard precautions primarily stop the spread of disease in the infection chain?

options.A: By interrupting modes of transmission and blocking entry
options.B: By destroying all infectious agents in the reservoir
options.D: By forcing pathogens to choose a non-human host

explanation: Handwashing and barriers block how germs travel and enter the body, stopping the infection chain. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h2)

question: When should a midwife choose soap and water instead of an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: Before entering a general antenatal room
options.B: Immediately after touching a clean bedside table
options.C: When rushing to assist an emergency delivery
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Soap and physical friction are required to wash away visible organic matter that alcohol rubs cannot clear. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h3)

question: What defines transient hand flora?

options.A: Harmless microbes that naturally protect skin
options.B: Bacteria that live permanently deep under the skin
options.D: Organisms picked up from touching contaminated surfaces or patients

explanation: Transient flora are picked up during daily tasks and are easily removed by proper hand hygiene. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h3)

question: Which personal protective equipment item should be put on LAST before a high-risk delivery?
explanation: Gloves are put on last so the clean barrier touches all other adjusted equipment right before patient contact. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h4)

question: A midwife expects heavy blood and fluid splashes during a delivery. What PPE combination is best?

options.A: Clean non-sterile gloves and a head cap only
options.B: N95 mask and thick utility gloves
options.D: Sterile gloves, fluid-resistant gown, surgical mask, and eye protection

explanation: High fluid exposure during delivery demands full coverage of hands, torso, mouth, nose, and eyes. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h4)

question: How should a midwife handle bed linen heavily soiled with amniotic fluid and blood?

options.A: Shake it vigorously to remove loose debris
options.B: Wash it by hand immediately in the nearest patient bathroom
options.C: Store it in an open bucket beside the station until evening
options.D: Place it directly into a leak-proof bag without sorting or rinsing

explanation: Minimizing handling and avoiding pre-rinsing prevents splashing and the spread of infectious aerosols. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h5)

question: Why must shared diagnostic tools like blood pressure cuffs be disinfected between antenatal clients?

options.A: To ensure the mechanical springs retain accuracy
options.B: To remove unpleasant sweat odours from hot weather
options.C: To prevent passive transfer of microorganisms between patients
options.D: To comply with sales tax regulations

explanation: Reusable items can pick up transient germs from one patient and transmit them directly to the next person. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h5)

question: What is the main danger of overfilling a sharps disposal box past its fill line?

options.A: Attraction of household pests into the room
options.B: Unpleasant odors spreading through the ward
options.C: Increased risk of accidental needle-stick injuries to staff

explanation: Overfilled safety boxes expose needles at the opening, making staff vulnerable to sharp punctures. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h6)

question: What is the recommended practice for recapping a used injection needle?

options.A: Bending the needle downward before insertion
options.B: Asking a colleague to steady the plastic cap
options.C: Holding the cap firmly with the opposite bare hand
options.D: Using a safe one-handed scoop technique

explanation: The one-handed scoop method keeps the non-working hand away from the sharp point, preventing punctures. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h6)

question: Which type of waste goes into a yellow bin marked with a biohazard symbol?

options.A: Empty cardboard delivery boxes and paper
options.B: Cotton swabs and dressings contaminated with blood or body fluids
options.C: Leftover food wrappers and plastic bottles

explanation: Infectious waste containing biological fluids goes into biohazard yellow bins for specialized destruction. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h7)

question: A midwife finishes dressing an infected perineal wound. Where should she discard the soiled gauze?

options.A: In the puncture-resistant yellow sharps box
options.B: In the black general household waste bin
options.C: In the yellow biohazard waste bin
options.D: In an open basin on her desk

explanation: Gauze soiled with body fluids and pus is infectious waste and must go into the biohazard container. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h7)
